```{python Navigation header, results='asis'}
import os

import report_utils as ru
from IPython.display import display, HTML

```

## Introduction

This report compares where IF2 ends up. Both implementations run the same
number of iterations from the same committed starting points
(`../starting_parameters.csv`) with the same perturbation sizes, so the
distribution of final parameter estimates should agree.

What varies within each run is the starting point; the seed varies too, so the
comparison is between distributions rather than between individual fits.

---

## Setup & Data Loading

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### System & Environment Information
```{python Environment Setup}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_density, facet_wrap, labs

os.environ["JAX_PLATFORMS"] = "cpu"

PY_DIR = os.path.join("results", "gpu")
R_DIR = os.path.join("results", "R")

py_results = ru.read_if_exists(os.path.join(PY_DIR, "results.csv"))
r_coefs = ru.read_if_exists(os.path.join(R_DIR, "mif_coefs.csv"))

missing = []
if py_results is None:
    missing.append(("pypomp results", os.path.join(PY_DIR, "results.csv")))
if r_coefs is None:
    missing.append(("R baseline", os.path.join(R_DIR, "mif_coefs.csv")))

print("pypomp:")
print(ru.format_metadata(ru.load_json(os.path.join(PY_DIR, "latest.json"))), end="")
print("\nR pomp:")
print(ru.format_r_metadata(ru.load_json(os.path.join(R_DIR, "latest.json"))), end="")
```

:::

```{python Missing sources, results='asis'}

```

```{python Build the long frame}
long_frames = []
if py_results is not None:
    long_frames.append(ru.wide_results_to_long(py_results, "pypomp"))
if r_coefs is not None:
    long_frames.append(ru.r_coefs_to_long(r_coefs))

combined = pd.concat(long_frames, ignore_index=True) if long_frames else pd.DataFrame()
combined = combined[combined["param"].isin(ru.LOG_PARAMS + ru.LOGIT_PARAMS)]
transformed = ru.to_estimation_scale(combined)
```

## Summary Statistics

Reported on the estimation scale (log for rates, logit for probabilities and
initial-state fractions), which is the scale IF2 perturbs on.

```{python Summary table}
summary = (
    transformed.groupby(["unit", "source", "param"])["value"]
    .agg(n="count", mean="mean", sd="std", min="min", max="max")
    .reset_index()
    .sort_values(["unit", "param", "source"])
)

display(HTML(summary.round(4).to_html(classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False)))
```

---

## Parameter Distributions

```{python Density plots, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}
for unit in sorted(transformed["unit"].dropna().unique()):
    unit_data = transformed[transformed["unit"] == unit]
    display(
        ggplot(unit_data, aes(x="value", fill="source", color="source"))
        + geom_density(alpha=0.35)
        + facet_wrap("~param", scales="free")
        + labs(
            title=f"IF2 parameter estimates: {unit}",
            subtitle="Estimation scale; one density per implementation",
            x="Parameter value",
            y="Density",
            fill="Source",
            color="Source",
        )
        + ru.scale_fill_premium()
        + ru.scale_color_premium()
        + ru.theme_premium
    )
```

::: {.callout-note}
### Expectation
The `pypomp` and `pomp` densities should cover the same region for each
parameter. IF2 from a scattered start is a stochastic search, so exact overlap
is not expected; a parameter whose two densities are disjoint is the signal
worth chasing.
:::

---

## Convergence Traces

```{python Traces, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}
from plotnine import geom_line, scale_color_gradient

traces = ru.read_if_exists(os.path.join(PY_DIR, "traces.csv.gz"))
if traces is None:
    display(HTML(ru.missing_note("pypomp traces", os.path.join(PY_DIR, "traces.csv.gz"))))
else:
    mif_traces = traces[traces["method"] == "mif"] if "method" in traces.columns else traces
    id_vars = [c for c in ["unit", "replicate", "iteration"] if c in mif_traces.columns]
    value_vars = [c for c in mif_traces.columns if c in ru.LOG_PARAMS + ru.LOGIT_PARAMS + ["logLik"]]
    long_traces = mif_traces.melt(
        id_vars=id_vars, value_vars=value_vars, var_name="param", value_name="value"
    )

    for unit in sorted(long_traces["unit"].dropna().unique()):
        unit_data = long_traces[long_traces["unit"] == unit]
        display(
            ggplot(unit_data, aes(x="iteration", y="value", group="replicate", color="replicate"))
            + geom_line(alpha=0.6, size=0.4)
            + facet_wrap("~param", scales="free_y")
            + labs(
                title=f"IF2 iteration traces: {unit}",
                x="IF2 iteration",
                y="Value",
                color="Start",
            )
            + scale_color_gradient(low="#3498db", high="#1abc9c")
            + ru.theme_premium
        )
```
